museum.network.about.title: A public museum for a network state
museum.network.about.description: How the 6529 Network holds, governs, documents, and is progressively decentralizing its public Museum.
museum.network.proposition.title: A public museum for a network state
museum.network.proposition.metadata: The 6529 Network Museum is a permanent collection of digital art held by the Network on Ethereum, governed through TDH, and open worldwide.
museum.network.proposition.intro: The 6529 Network is building a decentralized network state. The Museum is one of its first public institutions: a permanent collection of digital art held by the Network on Ethereum, governed through TDH, and open online to anyone in the world.
museum.network.proposition.principle: Public museums collect, preserve, and interpret the culture of a people. A network state should be able to do the same.
museum.network.proposition.ofNetwork.bod: The 6529 Network Museum is the Museum of the 6529 Network, held for public viewing.

Through TDH-weighted decisions, the Network sets collecting policy, authorizes programs and acquisitions, and determines how the institution develops. Editorial, registrar, technical, and operational work may be delegated, but it remains accountable to the Museum's public record.
TDH records participation in Museum governance. It carries no economic claim on the Museum's NFTs, and Network members hold no shares in its holdings.
A public museum may belong to a people while its works remain governed as one institutional collection. The 6529 Network Museum follows that principle on behalf of the Network as a whole.
museum.network.proposition.pillars.title: A network-native museum
The collection is held by the 6529 Network through a dedicated Museum Safe as one permanent institutional collection.
The Network holds the Museum. TDH provides the means by which it is governed.
museum.network.proposition.pillars.decen: Major collecting and policy decisions are made through TDH-weighted voting.
The Museum's public repository records and Museum Safe signers currently carry Network decisions into operation. The institution's next stage places more of its decisions directly in the network.
museum.network.proposition.pillars.ether: The Museum's accessioned artworks are NFTs held on Ethereum. Token identity, current custody, and transaction history can be independently verified from the chain and public record.
Ethereum records token identity and custody. Accession, legal title, copyright, artistic provenance, and preservation are established by the Museum's public record.

The next stage is to bring the institution itself further on-chain: its decisions should have a canonical Ethereum record, custody should be constrained by valid decisions, and approved actions should have a reliable path to execution.
The Museum is native to the internet. It has no fixed geography, opening hours, or physical threshold.

Anyone can visit with no wallet, membership, or invitation. The collection and its public provenance, policies, decisions, and governing rules are open to inspect. Donor privacy, personal data, legal files, and custody-security material remain separately controlled when required.
The Museum may be presented through many websites, applications, virtual environments, and physical exhibitions. No single interface constitutes the Museum.
museum.network.proposition.pillars.machi: The Museum's collection, accession records, provenance, policies, and decisions are published as structured public data as well as human-readable pages.
This supports independent verification and scholarship, and lets others build new interfaces independently of the current website.
museum.network.proposition.today.title: The Museum today
museum.network.proposition.today.body1: The Museum exists now. It has an accessioned collection, adopted collecting policies, TDH-weighted decisions, dedicated Ethereum custody, and a public, machine-readable institutional record.
museum.network.proposition.today.body2: It is meaningfully network-governed and moving toward fuller decentralization. Governance outcomes remain institutional records published by repository maintainers, while Museum Safe signers execute Ethereum transactions.
museum.network.proposition.today.collect: The accession register defines the permanent collection; the Safe's wallet inventory records custody. Accessioned works are held in the dedicated Museum Safe, with Ethereum custody and transfers independently verifiable.
museum.network.proposition.today.governa: The Network uses TDH-weighted voting for major collecting and policy decisions. Adopted effects and proposals awaiting adoption remain separate in the public record.
The repository is the Museum's current canonical institutional record and the bridge to an on-chain system. Its rules, records, revisions, and history are explicit, version-controlled, and open to inspect.
museum.network.proposition.next.title: The next stage
museum.network.proposition.next.intro: The next phase is to complete the connection between Network governance, the institutional record, and Ethereum execution. It requires three principal elements.
museum.network.proposition.next.decision: Approved Museum decisions should be recorded in a form that can be independently verified on Ethereum; their validity rests in the institutional record rather than an announcement, private database, or operating-team interpretation.
The Museum Safe should be technically constrained by valid Network decisions, embedding the Network's authority in the custody system itself.
museum.network.proposition.next.executio: A valid Museum decision should have a reliable path to the relevant Ethereum action, including an acquisition, transfer, or authorized mint, while keeping operator authority within the decision.
museum.network.proposition.next.conclusi: Together, these systems can join governance, institutional memory, custody, and execution while preserving clear limits on authorized effects.
museum.network.proposition.permanence.bo: The 6529 Network Museum is being designed to survive changes in websites, software, operators, signers, and service providers.

Permanence requires more than token ownership. Durable Ethereum state must be joined to content-addressed records, preserved media and software, rights and provenance evidence, migration paths, and interfaces that can be replaced.
The objective is that future stewards can reconstruct the collection, its decisions, and its institutional history even if the current website and operating team disappear.
museum.network.proposition.final.eyebrow: A public institution for the Network
museum.network.proposition.final.title: Culture, memory, and shared stewardship
museum.network.proposition.final.body1: A network state requires more than technical infrastructure. It requires culture, memory, and institutions through which shared assets can be governed and preserved. The Museum provides a practical place for the 6529 Network to develop those capabilities.
museum.network.proposition.final.body2: The art matters in its own right. The Museum is also an early working model of what a public institution created and governed by a decentralized network can become.
museum.network.proposition.final.closing: Nation states built public museums to hold culture in common. The 6529 Network is building that kind of institution for the networked world.
